subject: Capacity & SLA alignment for Clover commitment — tokens/sec, burst planning
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@clover.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity & SLA alignment for Clover commitment — tokens/sec, burst planning

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. As promised I'm sending a concise capacity-facing proposal so procurement and engineering can align on the committed footprint and SLA targets. High-level summary attached (redwood_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx) and a few questions below that will materially change the GPU sizing.

Short summary of our model assumptions (see sheet "Scenario A"):
- Peak sustained TPS (tokens/sec): 18k tokens/sec across the fleet (averaged over 60s windows)
- Typical request distribution: 60% short prompts (<=256 tokens), 35% mid (256-1024), 5% long (>1024)
- Target 95th pct latency SLO: <= 850ms for the chosen instruction model at 2k token generation average
- Model variant: open-llama-45b-quant (approx memory & KV profile in sheet)
- Autoscaling burst capacity for marketing spikes: additional 40% headroom for 30m windows

Key asks for Clover: please confirm or provide:
1) Realistic peak sustained tokens/sec and expected P95 latency SLO (we used 850ms above). If you need 500ms at 95th, the GPU count materially increases.
2) Expected concurrency profile (avg requests/sec, avg tokens/output per request) — the attached clover_token_profile.csv would help if you can fill it out.
3) Any data residency or private deployment constraints (we show Hosted + Reserved Dedicated mix in the spreadsheet).

Prelim capacity note: under these assumptions, the sheet estimates 12 x A100-80GB-equivalent slots for steady state and an additional 5x for burst (total 17 reserved slots), with an ops margin that maps to a 20% runway. This is illustrative; if you confirm a higher 95th latency target or higher long-tail prompt fraction the slot count will go up.

Next steps I propose:
- You loop in procurement (procurement@clover.ai) to start legal; I'll attach a stub MA for reference.
- If engineering can provide the token profile today we can re-run and give a concrete instance/zone sizing before EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx, clover_token_profile.csv

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

From: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@clover.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity & SLA alignment for Clover commitment — tokens/sec, burst planning

Ben —

Thanks — this is very helpful. Quick answers inline:

1) Peak sustained tokens/sec: our initial forecast for Q3 launch is ~14k tokens/sec sustained for business hours, with expected marketing-driven peaks of up to ~28k tokens/sec for 10-30 minute bursts during promotions.

2) Concurrency & token mix: average requests/sec ~160 RPS during business hours, avg output tokens per request ~90 tokens, but we do have some batch generation jobs that can be 1k+ tokens (approx 5% of requests). Filling clover_token_profile.csv and attaching.

3) Data residency: US-only for now, prefer Redwood Hosted + Dedicated reserved for production.

Latency SLO: product team prefers P95 <= 700ms if feasible; if not we need to understand the tradeoffs to 850ms.

I've attached the token_profile.csv (filled). Procurement is cc'ed. We'd like an updated sizing and a short note on expected unit cost impact if we raise SLO from 850ms to 700ms.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Kumar
Head of Product, Clover AI
aisha.kumar@clover.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity & SLA alignment for Clover commitment — tokens/sec, burst planning

Ben / Karthik —

I ran a quick pass on Ben's workbook with Aisha's real token profile. Highlights:
- Sustained tokens/sec for business hours maps to ~11k tokens/sec per the distribution Karthik usually uses to convert RPS->tokens; peak bursts (28k) are short but would push utilization past 85% on our conservative kernel selection.
- If we need P95 <= 700ms, we should target lower util per-GPU (target 65-70% instead of 75-80%). That increases reserved slot needs from 12 -> 16 steady-state, and burst slots from 5 -> 7.
- Recommendation: propose a 16-reserved + 6-burst configuration (22 total) to satisfy 700ms P95 with ~20% ops runway for on-call mitigation. Estimated committed monthly spend increase: ~28% versus the 12-slot plan.

I've attached a small sensitivity sheet inside the workbook (sheet "700ms_sensitivity"). Karthik, can you validate the kernel choices and expected tokens/sec per-slot used in the calc?

Laura
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@clover.ai>, procurement@clover.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity & SLA alignment for Clover commitment — tokens/sec, burst planning

Aisha / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the populated token_profile.csv — big help. Summary of the agreed proposal for procurement & legal:

1) Production commit configuration (recommended): 16 reserved slots + 6 burst slots (22 total) aiming for P95 <= 700ms for the model family we discussed.
2) Deployment mode: Hosted + Dedicated reserved capacity (US region).
3) Ops runway: ~20% buffer built into the committed capacity; automatic burst for 30-minute marketing spikes up to the 6 extra slots.
4) Cost delta: ~+28% monthly on committed spend compared to the 12-slot 850ms plan. Exact numbers in the workbook.

Attachments included for procurement: clover_signed_ma_stub.pdf (contract stub for internal review), redwood_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx (updated with 700ms_sensitivity sheet).

Next actions:
- Procurement: If that configuration looks ok, confirm and we'll generate a committed pricing term sheet and draft SOW.
- Aisha: We'll run a final validation on our infra testbed at the 28k burst number to validate latency tail behavior; planned window: Tue morning. Karthik / Laura will own the test.

I'll wait for procurement confirmation and will open a deal in HubSpot (link attached).

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
